messages:
maya (support): FYI escalation from customer on private/VPC deployment — ALB health checks showing Unhealthy for backend targets, API returning 502 from ALB but direct curl from bastion to pod is 200. Customer says only health checks fail, otherwise traffic ok.

alex (network): Which load balancer type and health check settings? path/protocol/host?

maya (support): Internal ALB, target type = instance -> forwarding to nodePort 8443 -> health check: HTTPS /hc interval 10s timeout 5s, healthy threshold 2. Host field is empty (ALB default uses IP). TLS on backends uses SNI and cert is wildcard for api.customer.internal.

alex (network): That could be SNI. ALB health checks by default set Host to IP which will not match cert. Can you repro from a node with and without Host header?

maya (support): Ran these from customer bastion (results pasted):
```
# works when Host matches
curl -v -H "Host: api.customer.internal" https://10.0.5.12:8443/hc --insecure
* Connected to 10.0.5.12 (10.0.5.12) port 8443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
> GET /hc HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.customer.internal\n\n< HTTP/1.1 200 OK\n\n# fails without Host -> SNI mismatch
curl -v https://10.0.5.12:8443/hc --insecure
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...\n* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name '10.0.5.12'\n* Closing connection 0
```

jordan (infra-oncall): Yep that's SNI. ALB health check needs Host header override set to the hostname that backend cert expects (api.customer.internal) or change health check to HTTP. Since customer policy disallows plain HTTP, we should update the target-group health check host.

alex (network): AWS CLI to modify TG: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn <arn> --health-check-host 'api.customer.internal'``` Also you can set this in console under Target Group > Health checks > Advanced. After that ALB will include that host in the health check TLS SNI and Host header.

maya (support): I also validated no SG or NACL blocks: ALB SG allows outbound to 8443, nodes SG allows inbound from ALB SG on 8443. Ran tcpdump on node while ALB healthcheck fired:
```
tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.0.5.12 and port 8443 -c 5
10:12:01.123456 IP 10.0.0.53.1024 > 10.0.5.12.8443: Flags [S]
10:12:01.223456 IP 10.0.5.12.8443 > 10.0.0.53.1024: Flags [S.]
# TLS Client Hello shown with SNI = (empty) before change
```

alex (network): Good catch. Once health-check host is set, ALB will send SNI and backend will present correct cert. That should fix TLS handshake and health state.

maya (support): Customer updated TG host as per suggestion, re-evaluating.

deploy-bot: Target group health checks transitioned to healthy for 8/8 targets (reason: TLS handshake successful) :white_check_mark:

jordan (infra-oncall): Confirming with customer — all APIs routed through ALB are now healthy and 502s cleared. Closing escalation.

maya (support): Customer confirmed production traffic normal. Leaving notes: for Private/VPC deployments using TLS on backend, ensure ALB health-check Host is set when cert expects SNI host; document in runbook. :memo:
